description: Width tiers for Dance — Foundation year level
subject: Dance

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single task context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Foundation Dance, minimum is typically one movement context, one audience sharing occasion, or one arts observation — sufficient to demonstrate the capability, not sufficient to show range.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope as ACARA intended at Foundation level. Grounded in the range of elaboration examples — covers the breadth of contexts a well-taught Foundation student would engage with.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new task contexts, stimuli types, cultural communities or performance settings. Must genuinely broaden the range of contexts — not deepen in a single context.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data for typical_width and to identify First Nations and cultural directions for wider. Foundation elaborations are cross-arts-form — dance-specific reading applied.

AC9ADAFC01.minimum_width: Create one simple movement sequence communicating an idea from lived experience — with a beginning and end.
AC9ADAFC01.typical_width: Create arts works across multiple forms (dance, drawing, sound) communicating ideas from personal or social experience; use digital devices to record; extend and vary known movements; manipulate objects and images to create or retell stories.
wider: Use stimuli from multiple modalities (music, tactile materials, imagery) as starting points for distinct movement creations — experiencing how different stimuli produce different movement ideas
Draw on stories and characters from students' own cultural communities as starting points — creating movement works that reflect community knowledge and experience
Use repurposed objects (clothing, boxes) to imagine and develop scenes — creating movement works that inhabit and transform the imagined environment
elaborations: creating arts works in a range of forms to communicate ideas from lived personal or social experiences
creating works in response to inspiration from sources such as play, imagination, observation, literature, artworks from their cultures and communities
extending and varying known songs, chants or rhymes
manipulating objects, puppets, 2D images and/or available technologies to create or retell stories
repurposing materials and objects such as clothing or packing boxes as starting points for imagining and developing scenes

AC9ADAFD01.minimum_width: Use play with movement prompts to discover at least two different ways of moving — noticing how movement can change.
AC9ADAFD01.typical_width: Use play, imagination and exploration to discover movement possibilities across multiple prompt types: tactile qualities of materials, imagery from stories, responses to music, geometric and organic shapes, improvised rhythmic patterns; discover speaking and singing voices; respond to emotions through movement.
wider: Use scarves, ribbons or props to discover movement possibilities — extending what the body can do with an external object
Respond to contrasting music styles and emotional moods through movement — noticing and describing how emotional response changes movement quality
Improvise movements to explain a process (steps in making something, growing something) — translating procedural thinking into physical expression
elaborations: playing with the tactile qualities of a range of materials and exploring how they feel to develop ideas for dance
imagining how characters in a story might dress or move, making still or moving images
identifying shapes, colours and lines in the environment and exploring ways to use these creatively
playing games to develop subject-specific practices; exploring ways that body parts, zones and bases can be moved safely and expressively
responding to emotions while listening to music and using movement to share responses
improvising rhythmic patterns for clapping or stamping or inventing new movements for familiar action songs
exploring speaking and singing voices and discovering ways to use them to communicate ideas and feelings
improvising movements to explain the steps in a process

AC9ADAFE01.minimum_width: Identify one arts experience from personal life and describe what it communicates or why it matters to the people involved.
AC9ADAFE01.typical_width: Identify and share arts experiences across multiple forms and cultural contexts; explore how facial expressions, gestures and movement communicate emotions; identify social and cultural dances that bring communities together; explore how illustrations communicate mood and narrative.
wider: Listen to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of arts for connecting to People, Culture and Country/Place — using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians
Explore dances and arts practices from students' own family communities — sharing these with peers and building a picture of arts diversity within the class community
Compare arts experiences from celebrations across two different cultural communities — identifying similarities and differences in purpose and participation
elaborations: exploring how facial expressions, gestures and other ways of moving communicate emotions and feelings in arts works
identifying and/or learning social or cultural dances that have meaning for people and communities, observing relevant protocols
identifying arts works and experiences in their lives and sharing ideas and feelings about them with peers and teachers
singing songs that are used for celebrations
exploring how illustrations in texts communicate narrative about characters, settings and mood
listening to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of the arts for connecting to People, Culture and Country/Place

AC9ADAFP01.minimum_width: Present a movement sequence to a small class audience; respond to one teacher question about what the work is about.
AC9ADAFP01.typical_width: Share arts works across multiple forms with audiences in gallery or performance walk formats; perform songs, soundscapes or movement sequences using learnt skills; use digital devices to record and document arts explorations; respond to teacher and peer questions about work.
wider: Use digital devices to record an arts exploration, curating a sequence of images or video to share — adding voice-over or commentary
Perform a movement/dance sequence created collaboratively with a partner or small group — introducing the shared work and explaining each person's contribution
Present retellings of stories using repurposed objects, toys or puppets — introducing the retelling to the audience
elaborations: sharing artworks with the class via a gallery or performance walk
performing songs, soundscapes or chants/raps using music skills
taking images of class arts events and creating an image sequence to document the occasion
talking about ideas such as themes, processes, or features of the work
presenting retellings of stories to peers through dramatic play using repurposed objects or puppets
performing movement/dance sequences created for other groups and introducing the work
using digital devices to record arts explorations
